chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a fish that leapt out of the river, fell onto the bank of the river, and died. Is it permissible to eat it? He said: If you catch it before it dies, then it dies, eat it; and if it died before you catch it, do not eat it.

key_terms.يَصْلُحُ أَكْلُهَا: it is permissible to eat it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish that die on the riverbank after leaping out of the water?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia juristic principle that fish are inherently halal and do not require ritual slaughter, provided they are captured while alive. It establishes a clear temporal criterion: if the fish is seized while still living, its subsequent death on land does not render it impure, whereas natural death prior to capture remains haram. This ruling underscores the distinction between marine creatures, which are exempt from the general 'slaughter' requirement, and other animals.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a fish which leapt out from the river, so it falls upon the bank of the river, so it died. Is it correct to eat it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you seize it before it dies, then it dies, so eat it; but if it died from before you seize it, so do not eat it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother, Musa ibn Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a fish that jumps out of the canal and lands on the side and it then dies: if it can be used for food. He (the Imam) said, ‘If you pick it up before it dies you can use it for food but if it dies before you pick it up, then do not use it for food.’”
